by the bed.text: "Stay in." She's the one out there, and she's telling me to stay in.

from the pack.text: Two cups. She packed for both of us. She knew I'd come.

on the post.text: Then I heard it again, from the trees. Okay. I won't answer. I won't.

torn page.text: Prints that just stop. She's describing mine. I haven't been to the pines yet. Have I?

the handwriting changes.text: That's my handwriting. That's how I make my M's.

don't turn around.text: Don't turn around. Fine. I won't. Just be at the lights.

intake.text: One cup. Just one. I'm not lifting that sheet. I'm not.

the grate.text: I didn't stack that wood. I know how I stack wood. This isn't how I stack wood.

the photograph.text: There's only me on the ice. I'm squinting at someone who isn't in the picture.

by the bed.text: She left the door open for me. Or for herself. She never could decide which of us needed rescuing.

from the pack.text: One cup. The intake said one cup. I'm not counting again. I'm not.

on the post.text: It used my name on her. And she answered to it. ...So would I.

torn page.text: Smaller than mine. Then not. Like the prints were growing into me.

the handwriting changes.text: Same hand, both pages. I'd know it anywhere. That's what scares me.

don't turn around.text: The sheet is the coat. Just the coat. Say it again. ...The sheet is the coat.

intake.text: The coat held its shape. Nobody was in it. ...Nobody was ever in it.

the grate.text: She signs her name the same as always. I just never let myself notice it before.

the photograph.text: One of us held the camera. In all these years I never once asked which.

door_stuck.text: Of course it's swollen shut. Of course today is the day it finally sticks.

door_free.text: There. Out. Whatever else waits out there, at least the door's done arguing with me.

stove_lit.text: There. One less cold room in this house.

window_latched.text: Latched. That's one less thing the storm gets to keep.

window_thread.text: A thread. Red wool, caught in the frame. She didn't leave through the door.

o_door.text: I... yes. The door was stuck.

o_after2.text: She stood right here. The snow didn't even notice.

n_wood.text: I was just... the wood. For the stove.

bedroom.text: Her side of the bed is still warm. She can't be far.

hall.text: Her boots are gone. The door isn't even latched.

living.text: Two chairs pulled out. She sat up with that candle until it went out.

backhall.text: Mathilda? She wouldn't go down there. She hates the cellar.

stair.text: If she's down here, she's been quiet a long time.

landing.text: No wind down here. Just my heart, and I wish it would slow down.

corridor.text: Why does a cabin need a hallway this long under the ground?

janitor.text: Someone keeps this place clean. Someone expects to use it.

morgue.text: No. She wouldn't be here. She's out in the snow. She has to be.

snow.text: Her prints are already filling in. I have to be faster than the snow.

lights.text: Headlights. Someone's waiting. Please let it be her.

lookout.text: Lanterns. Two lanterns on a rail. No car, no road. ...Follow the posts, she said. Not the prints.

lake.text: The lake. The ice is singing. ...I know this place.

bedroom.text: The lantern's still lit. Nobody's been here. Or I have, and I don't remember.

hall.text: I latched it behind me. I know I did.

living.text: Still two chairs. I keep thinking one of them will be pushed in.

morgue.text: I said I wouldn't come back down here. I keep coming back down here.

snow.text: Every set of prints out here could be mine.

backhall.text: Still only goes down. I keep hoping there'll be a back door this time.

stair.text: Nineteen. I checked again. It's still nineteen. Good. Good.

landing.text: Back down here. Like something in me keeps choosing it.

corridor.text: Same hallway. Same hum. You'd think I'd stop being scared of a hallway.

janitor.text: Clean again. Who cleans up after a thing like this? Who does that?

lights.text: Just the lanterns. I keep wanting them to be headlights.

lookout.text: Back at the lanterns. They haven't moved. I keep coming back like they might have.

lake.text: Still singing. It's waiting for me to walk out there.

dusk.text: It's getting dark. I've been out here all afternoon, and I'm still not where she is.

night.text: It's night. She's out in this, in the dark. So am I. That's something.

midnight.text: Midnight, or near it. If she's waiting for me, she's been waiting a long time.

dawn.text: It's getting light. I walked through a whole night and I still haven't found her.

late.text: It's nearly the hour I let her go. If I don't go to her now, I don't think I get to.

unready.text: Not yet. I can't go out there yet. I don't know enough of her to know what I'll find.

sighted.text: There. By the hole. ...Mathilda? Don't move. Don't you dare move.

hope.text: She knows this field better than I do. She'll have found shelter.
Ten minutes, she said. Ten minutes, and then the snow came in sideways.
When I find her I'm going to be so angry. And then I'm not letting go.
She always leaves something behind so I can find her. Always.
Every white shape is her coat, until it isn't.
She'll be cold. She never wears the hat. I should've made her wear the hat.
If she's sitting in some hunting hut eating my chocolate, I swear to God.
She hums when she's cold. Badly. I'd give anything to hear it now.
Okay. Think. If I were her, where would I go? ...Exactly where I told her not to.
"Go, then." Great. Brilliant. Best thing I've ever said.

doubt.text: Her prints stop. Mine don't. What does that make me?
I've said her name so many times it's just a sound now.
What if she's back at the cabin, by the lantern, writing to me?
I can't remember which of us said we'd stay.
I keep turning to tell her something. There's nobody to tell.
The light's going. She always said the afternoons up here end all at once.
My feet stopped hurting a while ago. I'm choosing not to think about that.
Sometimes I hear her footsteps right behind mine. Exactly in time. Exactly.
She always got to be the brave one. I got to be the one who waited. Who decided that?
On the lake the ice was singing, and someone held very still, and someone pulled. I don't remember which one was me.

resolve.text: Don't turn around. I can do that. I can do that much.
If she's behind me, she can see me. That has to be enough.
The engine's running. Someone kept it warm for one of us.
Whatever's at the lights, I'm walking up to it. I'm not stopping now.
I'll find you. Or you'll find me. One of us gets to go home.
I'm not cold any more. That's bad, isn't it. Keep walking.
If you can hear me, I kept the lantern lit. I did one thing right.
Don't be at the lights because something happened. Be there because you're stubborn. Please.
Thirty years of being careful, and look where it got me. A field.
I wrote "tell her" on a list. Like it was milk. Like there'd be time.

after.text: Just me. It was only ever going to be just me.
Hey. ...Hey. I'm here. I've got you.
I used to think she was the brave one. Maybe I just kept handing her my courage to hold.
One set of prints. Okay. Then they're mine to carry.
I'm so tired of being the one who stays.
Walk. Just walk. Both of us.

hope.text: When we first came up here the roof leaked, and we put every pot in the house under it. She played them like drums all night. I told her to stop. I wish I hadn't.
She steals my gloves. Every winter. Then she gives them back with the fingers stretched, like that's an apology. It sort of is.
She'd stand at the window in a storm with all the lights off. Said it was the only time the world was quiet enough to hear yourself. I always turned the lights back on.
Last time she got lost she came home with a stray dog and a story about a bear. There was no bear. The dog stayed eleven years.
She's done this before. Walked out angry, walked back in with snow in her hair, made tea like nothing happened. That's all this is. That's all.
Past the lookout there's a lake. We skated it every winter. She always went further out than I would, and waved, and I never waved back.

doubt.text: She said I don't live, I just keep house. I said at least one of us keeps anything. And she picked up the pack. And I let her.
There's a photo on the fridge where you can't tell which of us is which. Same coat, same hood. I used to think it was funny.
When I was small I had a friend nobody else could see. She did all the things I was afraid of. I don't know why I'm thinking about her now.
I keep doing the sums. How long without a fire. How long in wet socks. I keep getting a number I don't like, so I keep doing them again.
The last thing I said to her was "go, then." Not goodbye. Not be careful. "Go, then."
That winter the ice was singing. She said singing ice is safe ice. It isn't. It's the ice telling you it's thin.

resolve.text: If I find her, I'm not saying sorry first. I'm holding on until she complains. Then sorry.
The ice sang under us. Someone wouldn't move. Someone came across on their stomach and pulled. I've told that story both ways my whole life. Both ways are true.
Everything I didn't do, I gave her to do. Every risk. Every door. No wonder she's out here. I sent her out here.
If there's anyone under that sheet, they're wearing my coat. I know that. I've known since the cellar.
Just let it be the two of us at the car, arguing about who drives. That's all. That's all I'm asking for.
I had her by the collar. I remember the collar so clearly. I don't remember the face above it.

hope.text: Mathilda!
Mathilda! Can you hear me?
Mathilda! Over here!
Mathilda! It's me!
Mathilda! I've got your gloves!

doubt.text: Mathilda! Answer me!
Mathilda... where are you?
Mathilda! Say something!
Mathilda! Mathilda, please, answer me, please!
Mathilda! This isn't funny!

resolve.text: Mathilda! I'm coming!
Mathilda... please.
I'm going to the lights, Mathilda! Meet me there!
Mathilda... I'm sorry. Do you hear me? I'm sorry.
Mathilda! I'm not going back without you!

spent.text: I can't run any more. I can't.
Stop. Stop. You're no use to her like this.
Breathe. In. Out. Like she showed me.
Too fast. Too fast. Slow down.

cold.text: I can't feel my hands. That's fine. I don't need hands.
I can't see anything. I can't see... okay. Find a post. Find a post.
Coat, done up to the throat. Very sensible. Still freezing.
The snow's getting warm. That's wrong. Snow isn't warm.
She's out in this. She's been out in this all along.
Keep moving. Cold is just a feeling. Keep moving.

falls.text: I'm okay. I'm okay. Nothing's broken.
Get up. Nobody's coming to pick you up. Get up.
Stay down a second. No. Up.

turned.text: There's nobody. Just my prints. Only ever mine.

doubt.text: Go, then!

resolve.text: I'm right behind you.

misread.text: I want it to say that. It doesn't.
Right. Because that would make sense.
That's what I want it to say. Not what it says.
No. She'd never be that kind to me.
Not that. Read it the way she'd say it.

road.text: Mathilda? I've got you. I've got you. Hold still, I'm pulling.

prints.text: I'm sorry I sent you out there alone. ...Come on. Let's go home.

gone.text: Mathilda? ...Mathilda! ...I took too long. I always take too long.
